assertion: Johns Hopkins University laid off more than 100 employees in June 2026 after its federal research portfolio dropped by more than $500 million over the prior year.
independent_value: 110 employees laid off June 2026; JHU's own statement put the decline in its multiyear federal research portfolio's outstanding value at over $500 million for calendar year 2025

sources.title: Johns Hopkins University lays off over 100 employees, cites federal funding cuts

sql: SELECT year, institution, rd_expenditure_usd_thousand FROM research.nsf_herd_by_institution WHERE institution ILIKE '%Johns Hopkins%' AND funding_source='Federal' AND federal_agency='Total' AND rd_field='All' ORDER BY year
warehouse_value: Federal R&D expenditure: $2.97B (fiscal 2022), $3.32B (fiscal 2023), $3.62B (fiscal 2024); no row exists for fiscal 2025 or 2026
reason: Corroborated by independent news reporting and JHU's own Feb 2026 public statement; the corpus's own HERD table does not reach the relevant period.

assertion: In 2025, the National Institutes of Health (NIH) gave out 25% fewer new grants than it did in 2024, and NIH is behind that pace for 2026.
independent_value: NIH's own published figures: new/renewal competing RPG awards fell from 10,265 to 8,161 (a 20.5% decrease); R01-equivalent competing awards fell from 7,000 to 5,471 (a 21.8% decrease); total extramural awards fell from 59,063 to 55,394 (a 6.2% decrease)

assertion: The National Science Foundation's (NSF) number of new grants shrank 46% from the average during the Biden administration, to a level not seen since the 1980s.
independent_value: NSF new-grant count roughly 46% below the FY2021-24 average as of FY2026 (5,684 issued as of Aug 19, 2026, tracking to roughly 6,100 for the year), lowest since the early 1980s
